source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Feed the pregnant sow twice daily, gradually increasing the amount until 6–7 days before farrowing, then reduce the quantity by about 30% in that final week. Add green leaves (such as high-protein pasture or fodder-tree leaves) to boost protein intake. Let pregnant sows and gilts exercise in a large pen or paddock with access to shade and water. Treat for internal parasites one week before farrowing to prevent the sow passing parasites to her piglets and to help avoid 'thin sow syndrome'; treat external parasites (mange, lice) at 3 and 1 week before farrowing if present. A sow that loses more than 10% of her body weight between farrowing and weaning is unlikely to conceive again easily, so maintaining good body condition throughout pregnancy matters.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
